learning_objective: 🎯 Master the foundational language of chemistry! Learn how matter is classified, how to count invisible atoms using the Mole concept, and how to calculate recipe ratios for chemical reactions.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Chemistry follows strict rules! The Law of Conservation of Mass says matter cannot be created or destroyed. The Law of Definite Proportions says a given compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by weight (e.g., Water is always $H_2O$).
Atoms are too tiny to weigh normally. We measure them relative to a Carbon-12 atom (1 amu = $1/12$th mass of C-12). Molecular mass is simply the sum of atomic masses of all atoms in a molecule.

A 'Mole' is just a chemist's dozen. While a dozen is 12, a Mole is exactly $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ particles (Avogadro's number). The mass of one mole of a substance in grams is exactly equal to its molecular mass!
The Empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound (like $CH$ for Benzene). The Molecular formula gives the exact actual number of atoms (like $C_6H_6$ for Benzene).

Stoichiometry is using balanced chemical equations to calculate the exact amounts of reactants needed or products formed. The 'Limiting Reagent' is the reactant that gets completely consumed first, stopping the reaction entirely.

fun_activity.title: 🥪 The Sandwich Stoichiometry
fun_activity.instructions: If a sandwich requires 2 slices of bread and 1 cheese slice. If you have 10 slices of bread but only 3 cheese slices, how many sandwiches can you make? Only 3! The cheese ran out first—it is your 'Limiting Reagent'. Chemical reactions work exactly the same way!

exam_tips: 📌 Limiting reagent numericals are a guaranteed exam question. Always calculate the moles of each reactant first and divide by their stoichiometric coefficients to find the limiting one.
📌 Differentiate clearly between Molarity (moles/L of solution) and Molality (moles/kg of solvent). Remember: Molality does NOT change with temperature!
📌 Always use a tabular format (Element, %, Atomic Mass, Moles, Simple Ratio) to solve Empirical Formula questions to avoid calculation errors.
quick_recap: ⭐ 1 Mole of any ideal gas occupies exactly 22.4 Liters of volume at STP.
⭐ The law of multiple proportions was proposed by John Dalton (e.g., Carbon and Oxygen can form $CO$ or $CO_2$).
⭐ Precision refers to the closeness of various measurements to each other, while Accuracy is the agreement of a measurement with the true value.
